newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, March 21 - Customs in the shipping sector are reported to have gone on strike. Luanda - All clearance of goods for import and export have been halted. There is no cargo moving in/out of the port. Lobito, Namibe, Soyo, Cabinda - Reported as operating normally. Pilot and towage operations for vessels are currently operating. Delays to vessels are expected. All offshore crude terminals are operating normally, no berthing delays reported.

ISRAEL, March 25 - Haifa - 11 Vessels due, 2-3 days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, 6 general cargo, 3 bulk, 1 container, 1 tanker, 1 passenger. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 2 general cargo, 3 bulk, 1 container, 1 tanker. 2 Vessels under repair, 3 awaiting orders. Ashdod - Two to 4 days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, 10 general cargo, 2 bulk. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 15 general cargo, 1 bulk, 6 containers, 2 vessels awaiting orders. Eilat - One passenger vessel loading/discharging at berth.

MOZAMBIQUE, March 24 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restriction of 9.5 metres at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tugboat available. Beira - General cargo berths working normally. 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa. Some restriction for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres, 2 tugs available. General access channel - 2 Waverider buoys have been deployed in the approach channel. Each buoy is approx. diameter of 1 metre with flashing orange light with flash frequency of five one second flashes every 26 seconds.

Maputo - Berthing/sailing of 24 hours for vessels up to 120 metres loa. Some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths fluid. Draft restriction in the channel is 9 metres less 0.5 metres plus rise of tide of the day. Max. draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, March 24 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, March 24 - Durban - Container terminal - Delays of up to 48 hours for some vessels, whilst others berth on arrival. Point, New pier, Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Bunker supplies fluid, but this could change due to bunching of vessels. Drydock and floating dock fully committed until end of March. East London - No delays at general cargo/com terminal berths. Drydock fully booked until 30/3. Port Elizabeth - Two vessels in port, no delays on general, fruit, ore, tanker or container berths.

Cape Town - General cargo vessels working on arrival, 60 fishing trawlers due. Fruit berths fully occupied. Container terminal/bunker berths - no delays. Drydock and repair quay fully occupied. Saldanha Bay - Working normally. Richards Bay - General cargo berths fully occupied. The port will be closed from 1400 hours 27/3 to 0600 hours 29/3. Bulk import berths fully occupied until 5/4. Bulk export berths - Fully occupied. Bulk coal berths - 4 Vessels alongside, 6 anchored, 1 due on 25/3, 10 due by 31/3. Delays of 48 hours are currently being experienced.

TUNISIA, March 22 - Tunis - Five vessels in port of which 3 awaiting instructions, 1 discharging marble chips, 1 general cargo. Rades - Four vessels in port of which 3 ro-ro, 1 loading containers. Goulette - North side - 1 Passenger vessel, 1 general cargo. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 motor tanker discharging, 3 vessels in roads. Sousse - One vessel discharging bagged sugar, 1 vessel in roads, none awaiting orders. March 24 - Bizerta - Six vessels in port of which 1 discharging sugar, 1 discharging crude oil, 1 under repair, 2 loading steel, 1 loading cement. No berthing delays or congestion. Zarzis - No berthing delays or congestion.
